eyebrow: Guru–shishya parampara · Dakshineswar → Belur → the world
title: Sri Ramakrishna and his disciples
intro: Ramakrishna Paramahamsa was Vivekananda’s guru. This tree follows his direct disciples, their own disciples, and the people outside the order who said these teachings changed them.
note: Dates are birth–death unless marked. Influence lines record what the person themselves wrote or said, not membership of the order.

tree.name: Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa
tree.role: Priest of the Kali temple at Dakshineswar
tree.note: Learned Tantra from the Bhairavi Brahmani and Advaita Vedanta from the wandering monk Totapuri, who named him Ramakrishna. He also followed Vaishnava, Islamic and Christian practice and taught that every sincere path reaches the same God. He gave the ochre cloth to his young disciples shortly before his death at Cossipore in 1886.

children.name: Sri Sarada Devi
children.role: Wife, first disciple and spiritual mother of the order
children.note: Ramakrishna worshipped her as the Divine Mother in 1872. After his death the young monks treated her as their guru. She gave initiation to thousands, and the Udbodhan house in Calcutta was built for her.

children.name: Swami Nikhilananda
children.role: Founder, Ramakrishna-Vivekananda Center of New York (1933)
children.note: Initiated by Sarada Devi. His English translation of The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna (1942) is the version most readers in the West know.

children.name: Joseph Campbell
children.note: Helped Nikhilananda edit the English of the Gospel translation, and later travelled in India. He spoke of the work as a turning point in his reading of Indian thought.

children.name: J. D. Salinger
children.note: Read the Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna and attended Nikhilananda's New York centre. Vedanta runs through his Glass family stories.

children.name: Swami Vivekananda
children.role: Chief disciple; founder of the Ramakrishna Math and Mission (1897)
children.note: Met Ramakrishna in 1881 as a sceptical college student. Spoke at the Parliament of the World's Religions, Chicago, in 1893, taught Vedanta in America and England, and on return founded the Mission (1897) and Belur Math (1898). His motto: for one's own liberation and for the good of the world.

children.name: Swami Sadananda
children.note: Assistant station master at Hathras who left his post to follow the wandering Vivekananda in 1888.

children.name: Swami Swarupananda
children.role: First president of Advaita Ashrama, Mayavati
children.note: Edited the journal Prabuddha Bharata and translated the Bhagavad Gita into English.

children.name: Swami Shuddhananda
children.note: Translated many of Vivekananda's English works into Bengali.

children.name: Swami Virajananda
children.note: Ran Advaita Ashrama at Mayavati for years and led the order through the war and Partition.

children.name: Swami Kalyanananda
children.role: Founder of the Kankhal Sevashrama, Haridwar
children.note: Set up a hospital for sick pilgrims and sadhus in 1901 at Vivekananda's bidding.

children.name: Swami Paramananda
children.note: One of the youngest to take vows from Vivekananda. Later founded Ananda Ashrama in California.

children.name: Sister Nivedita
children.note: Irish teacher who met Vivekananda in London in 1895 and took vows in 1898. Opened a girls' school in Bagbazar, nursed plague victims, and backed Indian scientists, artists and nationalists.

children.name: Jagadish Chandra Bose
children.note: Nivedita edited his books and helped raise support for his research.

children.name: Abanindranath Tagore
children.note: Nivedita championed an Indian style of art and wrote in support of the Bengal School.

children.name: Sister Christine
children.note: Heard him in Detroit in 1894, came to Calcutta in 1902 and taught at Nivedita's school.

children.name: Josephine MacLeod
children.note: Called 'Tantine' by the monks. Travelled with Vivekananda and introduced many Westerners to the order.

children.name: Sara Chapman Bull
children.note: Widow of the violinist Ole Bull; gave much of the money for Belur Math.

children.name: J. J. Goodwin
children.note: Took down Vivekananda's lectures in shorthand. Most of the talks we have survive because of him.

children.name: Captain & Charlotte Sevier
children.note: English couple who met him in 1896 and built the Himalayan ashrama he had asked for.

children.name: Swami Abhayananda
children.note: One of the first Westerners Vivekananda initiated as a monastic.

children.name: Swami Kripananda
children.note: A journalist who helped organise the New York classes.

children.name: Raja Ajit Singh of Khetri
children.note: Paid for the voyage to Chicago. Tradition holds that he suggested the name Vivekananda.

children.name: Alasinga Perumal
children.note: Schoolteacher who raised the funds for Chicago and started the journal Brahmavadin.

children.name: Sarat Chandra Chakravarty
children.note: Recorded his talks with Vivekananda in Bengali as Swami-Shishya Samvada.

children.name: Mahatma Gandhi
children.note: Visited Belur Math in 1921 and said that reading Vivekananda had increased his love for his country a thousandfold.

children.name: Rabindranath Tagore
children.note: Told Romain Rolland that whoever wants to know India should study Vivekananda.

children.name: Sri Aurobindo
children.note: Wrote that during his imprisonment at Alipore (1908) he heard Vivekananda's voice guiding his practice.

children.name: Subhas Chandra Bose
children.note: Read Vivekananda as a schoolboy and called him the maker of modern India.

children.name: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
children.note: Hosted the still unknown monk in Pune in 1892.

children.name: Jamsetji Tata
children.note: Sailed with Vivekananda to America in 1893. His 1898 letter asking him to lead a research institute led towards the Indian Institute of Science.

children.name: Nikola Tesla
children.note: Met him in New York in 1896 and discussed the Vedantic ideas of prana and akasha.

children.name: William James
children.note: Met him at Harvard in 1896 and quoted him in The Varieties of Religious Experience.

children.name: C. Rajagopalachari
children.note: Said Vivekananda saved Hinduism and saved India.

children.name: Eknath Ranade
children.role: Builder of the Vivekananda Rock Memorial
children.note: Raised the Kanyakumari memorial (1970) on the rock where Vivekananda meditated in 1892, and founded Vivekananda Kendra (1972).

children.name: Swami Brahmananda
children.note: Ramakrishna called him his spiritual son. Vivekananda handed him the running of the order.

children.name: Swami Prabhavananda
children.role: Founder, Vedanta Society of Southern California (1930)
children.note: Translated the Gita and Upanishads with Christopher Isherwood. His Hollywood centre drew writers and thinkers.

children.name: Christopher Isherwood
children.note: Wrote Ramakrishna and His Disciples (1965) and My Guru and His Disciple (1980).

children.name: Aldous Huxley
children.note: Joined Prabhavananda's circle; The Perennial Philosophy (1945) grew from it. Wrote the foreword to the Gospel translation.

children.name: Gerald Heard
children.note: Brought Huxley and Isherwood to Prabhavananda.

children.name: Swami Yatiswarananda
children.role: Taught in Europe and America; vice-president of the order
children.note: Ran Vedanta work in Germany and Switzerland in the 1930s and in Philadelphia.

children.name: Swami Shankarananda
children.note: Oversaw the order's expansion after Independence.

children.name: Swami Shivananda
children.note: Known as Mahapurush Maharaj. Initiated a large number of the next generation of monks.

children.name: Swami Ranganathananda
children.note: Initiated by Shivananda in 1926. Lectured worldwide on the Gita, Upanishads and Vivekananda; awarded the Padma Vibhushan, which he declined.

children.name: Swami Akhandananda
children.note: Began the order's first famine relief, in Murshidabad in 1897, and ran an orphanage at Sargachhi.

children.name: M. S. Golwalkar
children.note: Lived at Sargachhi and received initiation from Akhandananda in 1937, shortly before his guru died.

children.name: Swami Vijnanananda
children.note: A trained engineer who supervised the building of the Ramakrishna temple at Belur Math. Lived mostly at Allahabad.

children.name: Swami Atmasthananda
children.note: Initiated by Vijnanananda in 1938. Led relief work in many disasters and headed the Rajkot ashrama.

children.name: Narendra Modi
children.note: As a young man spent time at Belur Math and the Rajkot ashrama and has called Atmasthananda his mentor; he was advised to serve society rather than become a monk.

children.name: Swami Saradananda
children.note: Wrote Sri Ramakrishna Lilaprasanga (Sri Ramakrishna, the Great Master) and built the Udbodhan house for Sarada Devi.

children.name: Swami Ramakrishnananda
children.note: Kept the daily worship of Ramakrishna's relics at Baranagar for years.

children.name: Swami Turiyananda
children.note: Went to America with Vivekananda in 1899.

children.name: Swami Abhedananda
children.role: Led the Vedanta Society of New York
children.note: Taught in America for about 25 years; later founded the Ramakrishna Vedanta Math in Calcutta (1923).

children.name: Swami Trigunatitananda
children.note: Built the Hindu Temple of San Francisco (1905), the first in the West.

children.name: Swami Premananda
children.note: Known for looking after every visitor and devotee at the Math.

children.name: Swami Yogananda
children.note: The first of the direct monastic disciples to die.

children.name: Swami Niranjanananda
children.note: Nursed Ramakrishna in his last illness.

children.name: Swami Adbhutananda
children.note: Came to Dakshineswar as a servant boy. Vivekananda called him Ramakrishna's greatest miracle.

children.name: Swami Subodhananda
children.note: One of the youngest disciples; did relief work in Bengal and Odisha.

children.name: Swami Advaitananda
children.note: Supervised the first works at Belur Math.

children.name: Mahendranath Gupta
children.role: Author of Sri Sri Ramakrishna Kathamrita
children.note: A headmaster who kept a diary of Ramakrishna's conversations from 1882. It became the Kathamrita, published in English as The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna.

children.name: Girish Chandra Ghosh
children.note: Father of the Bengali stage. A drinker whom Ramakrishna accepted as he was.

children.name: Nag Mahashay
children.note: Held up by Vivekananda as the ideal householder disciple.

children.name: Balaram Bose
children.note: His Baghbazar house was where the disciples met, and where the Mission was founded in 1897.

children.name: Suresh Chandra Mitra
children.note: Paid the rent of the Baranagar house, the first home of the young monks after 1886.

children.name: Gauri Ma
children.note: Started one of the first ashramas in Bengal for the education of women and girls.

children.name: Gopaler Ma
children.note: Saw Ramakrishna as Gopala. Spent her last years in Nivedita's house.

children.name: Yogin Ma
children.note: Gave Swami Saradananda much of the material for his life of Ramakrishna.

children.name: Golap Ma
children.note: Looked after the Holy Mother's household at Udbodhan.

children.name: Keshab Chandra Sen
children.note: Met Ramakrishna in 1875 and wrote about him in his journals, which first made him known to educated Calcutta.

children.name: Max Müller
children.note: Wrote Ramakrishna: His Life and Sayings (1898) with material supplied by Vivekananda.

children.name: Romain Rolland
children.note: Wrote The Life of Ramakrishna (1929) and The Life of Vivekananda (1930), which brought both to European readers.

succession.title: Presidents of the Ramakrishna Math and Mission
succession.intro: The order Vivekananda founded in 1897 has been led by a single president since Brahmananda. The first six were direct disciples of Ramakrishna or of Vivekananda. Click one to find them in the tree.
